speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources whether the Ministry will consider imposing a charge on plastic bags at supermarkets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: In Singapore, households generally reuse plastic bags to dispose of their waste in a hygienic manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: In addition, plastic bags which are thrown away are incinerated safely at our waste-to-energy plants before they are landfilled as ash.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This is in contrast to many other countries where waste is directly landfilled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: In these countries, plastic bags, which are not biodegradable, may remain in the landfills for a long time or find their way into the seas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Even though Singapore manages the disposal of plastic bags well, there is room for us to cut down on excessive usage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The recent discussions on the plastic bag issue reflect a greater environmental awareness among Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: I commend environmental groups for raising awareness on the need to curb the excessive use of plastic bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: I am heartened by recent media reports that major supermarket players in Singapore are open to considering measures to reduce plastic bag usage, such as a voluntary charge on plastic bags if imposed across the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: However, some concerns have been raised on implementing a plastic bag charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For example, will there be unintended consequences, such as the substitution of plastic bags with paper bags or even wastage of reusable bags?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Additionally, how can sufficient educational and enforcement measures be put in place to complement the charge and reduce demand for plastic bags by shoppers?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These will help in our formulation of any future policies on the use of different types of bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Ultimately, the excessive use of plastic bags can only be curbed with the support and participation of the community and retailers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Shoppers can play their part by taking just enough plastic bags for their needs and re-using them for bagging household refuse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: They can also utilise re-usable bags as much as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: With a strong partnership among the public, private and people sectors, I am confident that we can create a more sustainable Singapore together.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What we are calling for here is not a ban on plastic bags, which we know we need to use to bag our rubbish.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I think this is a pretty good middle ground.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is win-win because it is asking people to reduce the wastage, and the survey results so far show that people would reduce the wastage if there is just a 10-cent charge.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to thank the Member for his supplementary questions and comments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, we are looking at further measures to see how we can achieve this, as I have noted in my reply.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But let me also note that we need to recognise that our national circumstances are quite unique and different from those of many other countries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, concerns, for instance, regarding the non-biodegradability of plastic bags, which is really the key reason used to justify a levy on plastic bags in many other countries, really is not applicable in our context.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Moreover, we need to also recognise that the large majority of Singaporeans live in apartments, and they dispose of their refuse through the refuse chute, and they use plastic bags to dispose their rubbish in a hygienic manner.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It has taken us quite a long time to get this habit going.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The other thing is that if you look at the views on this issue, which is imposing a charge on plastic bags, it is actually quite mixed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Through our consultation as well as through the media and even social media, many are supportive of this, citing, for example, excessive use of plastic bags, as well as the fact that for countries that have used it, there is a significant reduction in the number of plastic bags used.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But there are also others who have objected, citing reasons like hygiene, in terms of disposing food in used plastic bags, as well as some unintended consequences that may arise.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, actually substituting the use of plastic bag with paper bags, which is also a resource.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, wastage of reusable bags and such.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are merits in the arguments on both sides.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We really need to do a study on this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, is it just major supermarkets or major retailers as well?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to do this before we come to a decision.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The idea is to look into how these different types of materials compare in terms of cost as well as environmental impact.
